reason: This passage (Joshua 2) records Joshua sending two spies to scout Jericho. The narrative follows their encounter with Rahab, their escape, and their return to Joshua. The passage concludes with the spies reporting favorably to Joshua, stating that the Lord has given them the land and that the inhabitants are fearful (v. 24). There is no complaint from any Hebrew leader about the people. Joshua does not voice complaints, nor do the spies. The tone is one of encouragement and successful reconnaissance, not complaint.
